spec.description: Screenshot capture pipeline stage telemetry (channel boxel:screenshot-perf): request records from the serving surfaces (realm-server) and capture records from the screenshot-card worker task, joined by jobId/correlationId. The same capture breakdown is persisted on media_cache_ledger.diagnostics for SQL reads.

panels.title: Capture-relevant requests (5m)

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:screenshot-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:screenshot-perf" | eventType="request" | realmURL=~".*${realm}.*" | surface=~"$surface" [5m])) or vector(0)

panels.description: Requests on the two capture surfaces that touched capture work: hits, renders, 503s, 403s. Addressing 404s/400s never emit.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service=~"realm-server|worker", env="$env"} |= "boxel:screenshot-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:screenshot-perf" | eventType="capture" | realmURL=~".*${realm}.*" | surface=~"$surface" [5m])) or vector(0)

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (count_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:screenshot-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:screenshot-perf" | eventType="request" | realmURL=~".*${realm}.*" | surface=~"$surface" [$__interval]))

panels.description: hit = ledger hit with zero Chrome work; rendered = capture completed within the sync wait; timeout/congested = 503 + Retry-After; gated = 403.

panels.title: Bucket size (CloudWatch)
panels.description: BucketSizeBytes for boxel-media-cache-${env}. The bucket deliberately has no S3 lifecycle expiry — the media_cache_ledger-driven deletes (the GC sweep and putMedia's repoint reclaim) are the only deletion path — so this panel is the growth watch. CloudWatch S3 storage metrics are reported once per day, so the value can lag up to ~48h; this panel spans 2d regardless of the dashboard range so lastNotNull always finds the newest daily sample. Shows 'No data' locally — CloudWatch is staging/production only.

panels.title: Bucket objects (CloudWatch)
panels.description: NumberOfObjects for boxel-media-cache-${env}, reported daily. Compare with 'Ledger object keys': the bucket stores one object per distinct object_key (dedupe-on-write), so the two counts should track each other; a persistent excess of bucket objects means orphans no ledger row references — invisible to GC, which scans ledger rows and never enumerates the bucket. Spans 2d regardless of the dashboard range so lastNotNull always finds the newest daily sample.

panels.title: Ledger-referenced bytes
panels.description: Sum of size_bytes over distinct object_key in media_cache_ledger — the bytes the ledger believes are in the bucket. A 'Bucket size' reading that grows persistently past this is leaked storage: reclaim deletes that failed (logged and swallowed) or objects written without a ledger row. Expect skew up to ~48h from CloudWatch's daily reporting before reading a gap as a leak.

panels.title: Ledger object keys
panels.description: COUNT(DISTINCT object_key) in media_cache_ledger — how many objects the ledger references. The bucket-object counterpart to 'Ledger-referenced bytes'.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT object_key) AS ledger_keys
  FROM media_cache_ledger;

panels.title: Bucket growth (daily)
panels.description: BucketSizeBytes (left axis) and NumberOfObjects (right axis) for boxel-media-cache-${env}, one CloudWatch sample per day. With no lifecycle expiry on the bucket, unbounded growth here means the ledger-driven GC chain (cron enqueue in the worker-manager → queue → media-cache-gc on a worker) is broken or leaking; check the stats to the left to tell leaked bytes from legitimate growth. Spans 30d regardless of the dashboard range so the daily samples form a trend.
